summary: U.S. equity futures opened cautiously Monday as investors digested last week's weak economic data and positioned ahead of a retail earnings wave. The dollar extended losses for a third session after July's disappointing retail sales and job losses reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in September. Futures on the S&P 500 traded near flat after the index posted its third consecutive weekly gain, while tech-heavy Nasdaq futures edged higher. In crypto markets, Bitcoin hovered near $62,700 and Ethereum near $1,875 as regulatory uncertainty persists following the SEC's unexpected cancellation of its vote on new crypto startup rules. Energy markets showed strength with oil prices up over 1% amid ongoing Middle East tensions, while the dollar index continued to weaken. Investor attention now turns sharply to retail earnings this week, with Home Depot, Target, Lowe's, and Walmart set to provide crucial insights into consumer health amid elevated inflation and weakening labor markets.

signals.title: Dollar Falls on Weak U.S. Economic Data, Fed Hike Bets Tumble
signals.desc: The dollar slipped 0.2% for a third day after weak retail sales and job losses reduced September rate-hike expectations, pressuring USD-sensitive assets.

signals.title: July Jobs Report Shows 23,000 Job Losses, Missing Estimates
signals.desc: The U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July versus expectations of 80,000-95,000 gains, signaling labor market weakness and raising recession concerns.

signals.title: Retail Earnings Wave Begins Tuesday Amid Consumer Spending Concerns
signals.desc: Home Depot reports Tuesday followed by Target and Lowe's, with consensus wary after July retail sales fell 0.6% and consumer discretionary stocks underperformed year-to-date.

signals.title: SEC Cancels Crypto Startup Rules Vote, Leaving Industry in Limbo
signals.desc: The SEC unexpectedly canceled its vote on new crypto capital-raising exemptions citing scheduling issues, delaying regulatory clarity for digital asset innovation.

signals.title: Binance Restricts 11 Exchanges Starting Aug 23 on Sanctions Compliance
signals.desc: Binance will halt transactions for HTX and 10 other platforms from August 23 following EU sanctions enforcement, potentially consolidating volume to compliant exchanges.

verdict: Markets face a defensive start to the week as weak economic data dampens Fed hawkishness, while retail earnings tests loom against a backdrop of deteriorating consumer fundamentals.
